meta.description: Complete IA redesign for Camp Concierge — a B2B SaaS for campground owners with a PWA guest app. This document defines the target navigation structure, content placement rules, feature consolidation logic, and UI pattern recommendations. Use this as ground truth when generating code, UI components, or further design documentation.

design_principles.principle: Ruthless consolidation — no feature duplication across navigation items
Intent-driven grouping — group by when/why the user needs a feature, not what the feature does
Progressive disclosure — secondary content is hidden until contextually triggered
Flat hierarchy — maximum two navigation levels; eliminate nested tab patterns
Single source of truth — each piece of data has exactly one authoritative location in the UI

failure.label: Five tabs answer the same question
failure.detail: Tabs Puls, Utforska, Planeraren, Aktiviteter, and Info all answer "what is there to do or know here?" This is one information need expressed across five navigation items, causing campers to check multiple tabs to feel confident they have complete information.

failure.label: Wi-Fi credentials duplicated across two tabs
failure.detail: Wi-Fi network and password appear on both Puls (tab 1) and Info (tab 5). This violates principle P5. Users learn to distrust both sources.

failure.label: AI Planner is a feature masquerading as a tab
failure.detail: Planeraren generates a time-blocked itinerary from existing Place data. It is a derivation of Utforska content, not an independent content category. Giving it a dedicated tab inflates navigation count for a single action.

failure.label: Hero section creates excessive visual overhead before any content
failure.detail: Sticky header + hero image + language switcher + weather pill + wind/rain pill + delayed feedback widget all load before the user encounters actionable content. Decoration is competing with function.

failure.label: Facility Manager is a permanent squatter inside Settings
failure.detail: Facilities are pinned to the bottom of Settings regardless of which Settings sub-tab is active. Facilities are a type of operational Place, not a configuration item. This is both wrong categorisation and a broken layout pattern.

failure.label: QR Code is hidden as a utility link outside the main navigation
failure.detail: The QR poster is the primary physical touchpoint that drives guest app adoption. Hiding it as a floating utility link — outside all nav groups — makes the most important marketing output the hardest thing to find.

failure.label: Settings uses nested pill-tabs inside a sidebar — double nesting
failure.detail: Settings contains four sub-tabs (Branding, Kontakt, Gästinfo, Anslag) rendered as pills within an already-nested sidebar. Announcements (Anslag) is a daily operational task trapped inside a configuration screen. This creates a "nested tab hell" pattern.

navigation.rationale: Campers operate in exactly two modes: (1) at-camp logistics mode and (2) out-exploring discovery mode. A third tab handles persistent saved state. Three tabs is the correct ceiling. Consider reducing to two tabs with Saved as a header icon.

element.contains: campground logo, camp name, current temperature
element.removed_from_here: language switcher (moved to gear icon), weather pill (condensed to temperature inline), wind/rain pill (removed — available inside place cards contextually)

element.rationale: Hero image, "good morning" text, and weather details add no navigational or informational value on a mobile PWA. The sticky header carries sufficient branding and context.

element.rule: Feedback prompt appears only after a user dismisses a visited place card, not on a timer delay after app load.

tab.name: Here
tab.intent: Everything a camper needs while physically present at the campground. Logistics, not discovery.

absorbs_from_old_architecture.source: Wi-Fi card, quick actions grid, announcements, facilities list, contact card
All content — phone, email, address, reception hours, Wi-Fi (deduplicated to single source here), checkout, trash, rules, emergency

section.label: Wi-Fi
section.constraint: THIS IS THE SINGLE AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE for Wi-Fi credentials. Must not appear on any other tab or section.

section.label: Quick Actions
section.pattern: Each item expands in-place (accordion) on tap. No navigation away.

section.label: Notices
section.filter: active announcements only; weather-relevant items surfaced first
section.note: Event-type announcements do NOT appear here — they appear in Explore tab under the Events category filter.

section.label: Facilities
section.note: Read-only in guest app. Managed by owner in dashboard under Places > Facilities tab.

item.name: See all info CTA
item.replacement: Redundant — this tab IS all the info

tab.name: Explore
tab.intent: Everything outside the campground boundary — discovery, planning, deals, and events. One surface for all outward-facing content.

absorbs_from_old_architecture.source: All place cards with categories, distances, open/closed status, heart/save, directions
AI itinerary generation — demoted to a triggered feature, not a tab
Events (surfaced via category filter), partner promotions (integrated as flagged cards in the place list)

primary_surface.type: categorised place list with filter pills
primary_surface.categories: Swim & Cafe, Food & Drink, Activities & Fun, Nature & Culture, Essentials, Events
primary_surface.place_card_fields: image, emoji, name, distance_meters, open_closed_status, owner_tip, is_partner_boolean, partner_badge_if_true

partner_card_treatment.rule: Partner cards are Place cards with a visual badge (e.g. "Partner offer") and an additional "Reveal discount" action that shows the coupon code. They appear inline in the category-filtered list — NOT in a separate section or tab.

events_filter_behaviour.rule: When "Events" category pill is selected, the list shows announcement items of type="event" from the owner dashboard. These are NOT shown on Tab 1 (Here).

ai_planner_feature.trigger: Floating Action Button labelled "Plan my day ✦" — visible on Explore tab only
ai_planner_feature.pattern: BOTTOM SHEET — slides up over the current list, preserving context. Does NOT navigate to a new tab or page.

sheet_content.conditional_banner: Rain warning with indoor place recommendations
sheet_content.note: Each timeline block references existing Place records. AI-generated descriptions and tips are attached to the place card within the sheet.

tab.name: Saved
tab.intent: Persistent list of places the camper has hearted. Lightweight — no additional content.
tab.content: List of Place cards the user has saved via the heart action in Tab 2.
tab.upgrade_path: If the product team wants to reduce to 2 tabs, move Saved to a heart/profile icon in the sticky header. This is the recommended future direction.

navigation.rationale: Owners visit the dashboard for one of three intent modes: (1) daily operations — checking analytics, managing places, posting announcements; (2) initial setup — configuring branding, contact details, guest info; (3) growth actions — managing partner deals, generating QR codes. The sidebar groups by these three modes, not by feature type.

page.sections: time_period_selector, kpi_cards_4, area_chart, language_breakdown, saved_places_list, secondary_kpis, top_tabs_list, map_directions_list, recent_feedback

tab_content.add_place_form_fields: name, address, category, on_site_toggle, indoor_toggle, custom_hours

tab_content.source_of_truth_for: facilities previously stranded in Settings page bottom section
tab_content.rationale: Facilities are a type of on-site Place. They belong here, not in Settings. Moving them here removes the permanent-squatter pattern from Settings.

page.source_of_truth_for: announcements previously buried inside Settings > Anslag sub-tab
page.rationale: Owners post announcements frequently (weather alerts, events, notices). This is a daily operational task and must be a top-level nav item, not a Settings sub-tab.

page.fields: wifi_network_name, wifi_password, checkout_textarea, trash_textarea, camp_rules_textarea, emergency_info_textarea
page.note: Wi-Fi credentials entered here are surfaced in Guest App Tab 1 (Here). This is the single edit point for Wi-Fi data.

page.partner_card_fields: logo, name, priority_rank, active_status, description, coupon_code, total_clicks
page.partner_form_fields: business_name, description, coupon_code, website, phone, logo_url, link_to_place_dropdown, priority_rank, start_date, end_date
page.note: Partners remain a separate management page from Places, but are rendered as augmented Place cards in the Guest App. The link_to_place_dropdown in the form is the data join between the two entities.

page.source_of_truth_for: previously hidden utility link "QR-kod" — promoted to primary nav
page.rationale: The QR poster is the primary physical mechanism for driving guest app adoption. It must be a first-class nav item under Grow, not a hidden utility link. Renaming to "QR & Share" reinforces its marketing function.

left_column.label: Controls
left_column.fields: template_picker, background_color, text_qr_color_with_contrast_warning, toggle_show_camp_name, toggle_show_slogan, slogan_text_input, qr_size_selector, paper_format_selector

element.reason: Dissolved into three focused standalone pages: Branding, Contact & Hours, and Guest Info. The nested pill-tab pattern inside Settings is eliminated entirely.
Announcements promoted to top-level Daily Ops nav item.
Facilities moved to Places > Facilities tab.
QR promoted to primary nav item QR & Share.
Moved to a persistent secondary action button in the dashboard header/topbar — always accessible, not buried.

pattern.name: Bottom Sheet (Pull-up Panel)

case.trigger: Plan my day FAB on Explore tab

pattern.behaviour: Slides up from bottom of viewport. Background content remains visible but dimmed. Dismissible via swipe down or backdrop tap. Does NOT trigger full-page navigation. Preserves user's scroll position in the underlying list.
pattern.implementation_notes: Use a detent/snap system: short content snaps to 40% viewport height, long content (AI planner) snaps to 85%. Always include a drag handle. Trap focus inside sheet when open for accessibility.

pattern.name: Contextual FAB (Floating Action Button)

case.label: + New Place
case.action: opens add place form (inline expansion or bottom sheet on mobile)

pattern.behaviour: FAB is context-aware — it reflects the primary creation action of the current page. It is NOT a global FAB that opens a menu of options. One page, one FAB, one action. The Explore tab FAB is the only exception where the action is generative (AI) rather than additive (CRUD).
pattern.implementation_notes: On desktop Owner Dashboard, inline "New [entity]" buttons in the page topbar are preferred over a FAB. FAB is a mobile-first pattern. Use the Explore tab FAB to create visual hierarchy that signals AI capability without adding a tab.

pattern.name: Accordion Inline Edit (Expand-in-Place)

case.content: Edit form expands inline below the card header

case.trigger: Tap on Checkout / Trash / Rules / Emergency
case.content: Info text expands inline below the button

pattern.behaviour: Clicking Edit expands the card in-place to reveal form fields. The card does not navigate away to a detail page. Saving collapses the card back to its summary state. At most one card is expanded at a time — expanding a second card collapses the first. On mobile viewports (<640px), the inline edit pattern falls back to a Bottom Sheet (UP1).
pattern.implementation_notes: Animate the height expansion with a CSS transition (max-height: 0 to max-height: [computed]). Use a subtle left border accent in the brand color to visually indicate "edit mode" state. Cancel button must be prominently accessible without scrolling.

flow.rule: Single write point in dashboard. Single read point in guest app. No other location in either interface should display or allow editing of these values.

Event-type announcements are surfaced in Explore under the Events filter. Info and Warning types are surfaced in Tab 1 Here under Notices. Type determines which tab in the guest app receives the content.

flow.source_field: owner_dashboard > partners > active partner records with linked place_id
flow.destination: guest_app > tab_2_explore > place cards with is_partner = true
flow.rule: A Partner record linked to a Place ID causes that place card in the guest app to render with a partner badge and a "Reveal discount" action. Inactive partners do not affect the guest app display.

flow.source_field: owner_dashboard > places > facilities tab > facility list
flow.rule: Facilities are edited exclusively in the owner dashboard Places > Facilities tab. Read-only in guest app.

Branding values cascade to the guest app's visual theme. Hero image is used as a decorative element only if the product team reintroduces a reduced hero in a future iteration — not in the current redesign.
